headline: Clinton order creates a White House task force on drug use in sports and names the drug policy director to the World Anti-Doping Agency board.
what_it_does: This order sets up a White House Task Force on Drug Use in Sports. It also allows the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy to serve as the U.S. government's representative on the board of the World Anti-Doping Agency, an international group that works on rules against performance drugs in sports. No summary was provided, so details about the task force's members and duties are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy
who_it_affects.how: The director is authorized to represent the U.S. government on the World Anti-Doping Agency's board.

who_it_affects.group: Federal officials named to the task force
who_it_affects.how: They take part in a new White House group focused on drug use in sports.
They may be affected by U.S. government work on anti-doping policy through the task force and the World Anti-Doping Agency.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed August 9, 2000; exact effective date not stated in the source.
